source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἐν τῇ Τεσσαρακοστῇ τῇ ὑστέρᾳ ἑβδομάδι τὴν πέμπτην λύειν, καὶ ὅλην τὴν Τεσσαρακοστὴν ἀτιμάζειν· ἀλλὰ δεῖ πᾶσαν τὴν Τεσσαρακοστὴν νηστεύειν ξηροφαγοῦντας.
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is decreeing how the Lenten fast must be kept, continuing from the previous canon about not offering bread except on Sabbath and the Lord's Day.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary in the last week of Lent to break the fast on the fifth day, and to dishonor the whole of Lent; but it is necessary to fast the whole of Lent, eating dry food.

choices.why: The adjective ὑστέρᾳ means 'later/last' and here modifies the week of Lent, so 'last week' is the plain literal sense.
πέμπτην is the ordinal 'fifth' used substantivally for the fifth day of the week, Thursday; keeping 'fifth day' preserves the source's numerical expression.
The participle means eating dry or uncooked food, a technical term for a strict fast; 'eating dry food' is the literal rendering.
The verb means to treat as without honor; 'dishonor' keeps the moral force of the council's charge.

pass_b_english: It is not right to break the fast on the fifth day of the last week of Lent, and so dishonor the whole of Lent. Instead, one must fast throughout all of Lent, eating dry food.

last_rejected.why: ξηροφαγοῦντας means eating dry foods (bread, salt, vegetables, no oil/wine), not merely 'dry food' as a noun phrase; the participial force is lost.
last_rejected.fix: keeping to a diet of dry foods
last_rejected.ruling: ξηροφαγοῦντας = 'eating dry food'; singular vs plural 'foods' is negligible, and English participle preserves the participial force adequately.
